 Judgment

Dated this the 05th day of March, 2025 This Land Acquisition Appeal is filed by the appellant/2 nd claimant in L.A.R.No.487 of 2010 of the II Additional Sub Court, Thiruvananthapuram, challenging the judgment and decree dated 06.11.2015.

Parties are hereinafter referred to by their respective status in the L.A.R.
2.

An extent of 0.22 (0.12 + 0.10) Ares of land comprised in Sy.No.1875 (LA Re-Survey No. 1875/9)
of Vanchiyoor Village in Thiruvananthapuram Taluk for widening Pattoor- Choorakkattupalayam road.
The 2nd claimant was the owner of the said 0.10 Ares of land.
The 0.12 Ares of land belonged to her brother, viz., the 1st claimant in the L.A.R.
The date of notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was 21.11.2007.
The award was passed on 20.05.2009 for an amount of Rs.1,56,127/- as compensation.
The land was taken possession of on 30.05.2009.
The 2nd claimant received Rs.76,942/- under protest.

Dissatisfied with the total compensation, the 2 nd claimant along with 2025:KER:18293 her brother viz., the 1st claimant in the L.A.R., preferred a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The reference court dismissed the L.A.R. inter alia holding that the claimants had failed to appear or to be represented and also that no evidence had been tendered to show that the compensation granted was inadequate.
This L.A.A. is filed by the 2nd claimant challenging the said dismissal.

sentences.text: 3. Heard Sri
. D.Ganesh Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant/2nd claimant and Smt.Rekha C.Nair, learned Senior Government Pleader for the respondents/respondents.
4. The land value awarded by L.A.O. for 0.10 Ares of the 2 nd claimant is (0.10x Rs.4,44,867/- per Are) Rs.76,942/-.
The enhanced compensation sought by the 2nd claimant based on the judgment in L.A.R.No.474 of 2010 (0.10x Rs.27,50,000/- per Are) is Rs.2,75,000/-.
The learned counsel for the 2 nd claimant proceeded to substantiate the said claim relying on Annexures A1, A2 and A3 documents produced at the appellate stage.

It is contended that the 2nd claimant is legally entitled to enhanced compensation since the same had been awarded to properties acquired under the same 2025:KER:18293 notification and the same reference.
Reliance is placed on the judgment in L.A.R.No.474 of 2010 (Annexure A1) and in L.A.R.No.443 of 2010 (Annexure A2).
Reliance is also placed on the judgment of this Court in L.A.A.No.337 of 2015 (Annexure A3).
Properties situated in Annexures A1 and A2 are situated on the immediate south and north of the property of the 2 nd claimant covered in L.A.R.No.487 of 2010.
They are similar and identical properties acquired for the same purpose.

Section 4(1) notification was published on 21.11.2007 and the award was passed on 20.05.2009 and the property was taken possession of on 30.05.2009 with respect to L.A.R.No.474 of 2010, L.A.R.No.443 of 2010 and L.A.R.No.487 of 2010
are the same.
5. It is noted that L.A.R.No.474 of 2010 concerns property adjacent property to the property of the 2 nd claimant.
The land value was fixed therein at Rs.27,50,000/- per Are.
The same was followed in L.A.R.No.245 of 2010 as well as L.A.R.No.443 of 2010 which were under the same notification and category and same purpose.
The land value was fixed therein too is Rs.27,50,000/- per Are.
The judgment and decree in L.A.R.No.443 of 2010 were challenged by 2025:KER:18293 the State before this Court in L.A.A.No.337 of 2015.
The said L.A.A. was dismissed by this Court vide Annexure A3 judgment dated 09.12.2015.

It was finally concluded by this Court that there was no reason to interfere with the fixation of land value at Rs.27,50,000/- per Are.
6.

In view of the above, the fixation of land value at Rs.27,50,000/- per Are has become final and the 2 nd claimant is entitled to land value at the same rate commensurate to the extent of property acquired from her.
She will also be entitled to all the statutory benefits from 21.11.2007 onwards as had been granted to the claimants in L.A.R.No.474 of 2010.

However, she shall not be entitled to interest on the said amount for a period of 1490 days of delay in filing the L.A.A. vide order dated 22.11.2024 in C.M. Application No.1 of 2021 in L.A.A.No.138 of 2021.
L.A.A. is allowed as above.
